source.title: Efficient shallow learning as an alternative to deep learning
source.authors: Yuval Meir; Ofek Tevet; Yarden Tzach; Shiri Hodassman; Ronit D. Gross; I. Kanter

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary information are present. Some equations and table headings are garbled or flattened, but the results relevant to this record are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests error scaling in CIFAR-10 image-classification networks, an image-model setting beyond text pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study measures CIFAR-10 test classification error against convolutional filter count, not language-model held-out cross-entropy against parameters, tokens, or compute. It does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, downstream language-task predictability, or architecture effects at fixed parameter count. The MAdds calculations and complexity extrapolations are not rows for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to CIFAR-10 test error against filter count for trained CNNs (LeNet, VGG-16), so its own results bear on whether the scaling form holds for image models (V5). It also shows the fitted exponent shifting with filter-allocation setup (V7). It does not measure language-model loss, tokens or compute allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that test error decays as a power law in first-layer filter count (ρ≈0.4) for both generalized LeNet and VGG-16 on CIFAR-10, and they call this hinting at universal behavior. By extrapolation, they argue a shallow LeNet could reach deep-learning error rates at lower per-step complexity. They find the conservation law asymptotically minimizes error. They call for further testing on other architectures and databases.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image-classification CNNs and measures test error against filter count; it does not use language-model pretraining loss or parameter/token/compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponent and pre-factor vary with convolutional filter-ratio settings; reported exponents include approximately 0.4, 0.35, and 0.32.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal filter allocation (conservation ratio) depends on the target error: larger ratios give lower error at small d but higher error asymptotically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The best architecture allocation for minimizing error depends on the scale or target error regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-input compute (MAdds) versus extrapolated error scales as ε^-5 for both nets; LeNet needs about 0.6× VGG compute per step.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute cost to reach a target error follows a power law derived from the error-vs-width exponent.

record.problems: The evidence concerns CIFAR-10 classification error rather than language-model cross-entropy. Some large-network results are described as preliminary or extrapolated; the authors state that further simulations on other architectures and databases are needed. At least 10 samples were used for simulation statistics.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant filter-scaling results were left out. Complexity and MAdds results were excluded because they do not measure the versions' named loss or performance outcomes.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Prediction of much larger LM runs from small-run fits. The only out-of-range point (LeNet d1=27, ε≈0.137) is a preliminary image-model result just 1.5× beyond the sweep.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count. Filter-ratio changes here also change parameter count.
Video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer. Data-size or compute scaling of image models. Cross-entropy loss rather than classification error. Scaling ranges beyond ~1.3 orders of magnitude.
Parameter-counting conventions, schedules, data, fitting-method choices. Disagreement among published LM laws.

missing.what: Raw ε values for the off-ratio LeNet and VGG sweeps. Rows only carry the text's approximate exponents.
missing.locator: Supplementary Information, raw data of Figure 4A/4B

missing.what: Preliminary LeNet d1=27, d2=72 result (ε≈0.137) close to the extrapolated power law
Enhanced VGG-16 (fifth set doubled, d=16): ε 0.0937 vs 0.11 original, a setup change affecting error

record.verdict_notes: The reader labeled V7 limits_scope, but exponent dependence on setup is what V7 asserts, so it is relabeled supports. Rows r3/r6 are power-law interpolations, not measurements. LeNet's original d1=6 point (0.236) matches the text. Exponent checks from SI data: LeNet ≈0.39, VGG ≈0.41.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between language-model parameters and tokens.
Architecture effects on loss at fixed parameter count.
The study tests image classification models on CIFAR-10 only; it does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other training regimes.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.

Only changes to convolutional filter-ratio setup are examined; the study does not test parameter-counting conventions, data choices, training schedules as a source of exponent differences, or alternative fitting methods.

relationships.condition: Generalized LeNet (d1 1–18) and VGG-16 (d 8–64) on CIFAR-10 with the conservation-law filter ratio
relationships.reason: Test error falls along a log-log line with ρ≈0.4 for both nets (LeNet 0.498→0.159; VGG 0.150→0.064), r1–r14.
relationships.display_finding: Test error followed power laws with ρ ≈ 0.4, decreasing from 0.498 to 0.159 for LeNet and 0.150 to 0.064 for VGG-16.

relationships.condition: Narrow scaling range and classification error as the measure
relationships.reason: The sweeps span only ~1.3 (LeNet) and <1 (VGG, 3–4 points) orders of magnitude in filter count, and the measure is test error, not loss (r8–r14, r17–r18).
relationships.display_finding: Filter sweeps covered approximately 1.3 orders of magnitude for LeNet and less than one for VGG, with only 3–4 VGG points and test error as the outcome.

relationships.condition: Off-conservation filter ratios in LeNet (4/3, 16/3) and VGG-16 (1.5, 2.5)
relationships.reason: A power-law form still fits each variant, with ρ≈0.32–0.41 (r15–r18).
relationships.display_finding: Each alternative filter-ratio variant retained a power-law fit, with ρ ≈ 0.32–0.41.

relationships.condition: Changing filter allocation across convolutional layers
relationships.reason: The exponent shifts from ~0.4 to ~0.35/0.32, and the prefactor changes with the setup, so fitted laws depend on architecture choices (r15–r18).
relationships.display_finding: Changing filter allocation shifts the exponent from approximately 0.4 to approximately 0.35 or 0.32 and also changes the prefactor.
